dbt-medallion-p01.script: Today we look at the medallion architecture: three layers called Bronze, Silver, and Gold.

dbt-medallion-p02.script: Silver holds cleaned data, and Gold holds business-level tables such as daily aggregates.

dbt-medallion-p03.script: Bronze stores raw data exactly as it arrived from the source, including rows with errors.

dbt-medallion-p04.script: Because Bronze is unchanged, we can replay and reprocess it when a cleaning rule changes.

dbt-medallion-p05.script: A dbt model is a select statement in a dot s q l file. The ref function points to another model.

dbt-medallion-p06.script: Please look at the slide on screen.

segments.objective: Explain the purpose of the Bronze, Silver and Gold layers
Explain why the Bronze layer keeps raw data unchanged

q-01.text: A source system sent some rows with wrong timestamps. What should happen to these rows in the Bronze layer?

options.A: Keep them exactly as they arrived
options.B: Fix the timestamps before loading them into Bronze

q-02.text: Which layer is the best place to audit what a source really sent?

segments.objective: Build dbt models with ref() and add dbt tests

q-03.text: Where do you declare a unique test for a dbt model?

options.A: In a SQL comment inside the model
options.B: In the schema.yml file next to the model

M-01.label: Bronze is cleaned
M-01.description: Thinks Bronze should already hold cleaned data

M-02.label: Delete bad rows
M-02.description: Thinks bad rows should be thrown away instead of kept for reprocessing

M-03.label: Skip to Gold
M-03.description: Thinks raw rows can go straight to the business-level layer

M-04.label: Tests in model SQL
M-04.description: Thinks dbt tests are written inside the model SQL

M-05.label: Tests in the orchestrator
M-05.description: Thinks dbt tests are declared in the scheduler

M-06.label: Tests in the dashboard
M-06.description: Thinks data tests live in the reporting layer

R-01.title: Bronze is a raw copy, cleaning happens in Silver
R-01.text: Bronze keeps raw data exactly as it arrived, including rows with errors. Errors found in Bronze are fixed or filtered in Silver, not in Bronze.

R-02.title: Do not delete raw rows
R-02.text: We keep raw data unchanged in Bronze so we can replay and reprocess it later when a cleaning rule changes. Deleted rows cannot be reprocessed.

R-03.title: Gold is built from Silver
R-03.text: The Gold layer holds business-level tables built from Silver. Raw rows first land in Bronze and are cleaned in Silver.

R-04.title: Where dbt tests live
R-04.text: Generic tests such as unique and not null are declared in a schema dot y m l file next to the model, not inside the model SQL.

R-05.title: dbt declares its own tests
R-05.text: dbt tests are declared in a schema dot y m l file next to the model, and running dbt test reports every row that fails.

R-06.title: Tests check data quality before dashboards
R-06.text: dbt tests check data quality on the models themselves. They are declared in a schema dot y m l file next to the model.
